key.name: tor-service
key.description: Name of the systemd unit that runs the Tor daemon, for example tor.service or tor@default.service.

key.name: socks-port
key.description: Port on which Tor exposes its SOCKS proxy on localhost.

key.name: manage-proxy
key.description: Switch GNOME proxy settings to Tor while it is running and restore them afterwards.

key.name: restore-proxy
key.description: Restore the proxy configuration that was active before Tor was started. If disabled, the proxy mode is set to “none” when Tor stops.

key.name: disable-proxy-on-stop
key.summary: Disable the proxy when Tor stops
key.description: Set GNOME’s proxy mode to “none” when Tor stops, even if a previous proxy configuration was saved. This takes precedence over restoring the previous settings.

key.name: start-tor-on-enable
key.summary: Start Tor when the extension is enabled
key.description: Start the configured Tor unit when TorShell is enabled, but only if Tor is not already running.

key.name: notify-state-change
key.description: Show a desktop notification when the Tor daemon starts or stops.

key.name: show-panel-button
key.description: Show the TorShell icon in the top bar.

key.name: panel-position
key.description: Side of the top bar where the TorShell icon is placed.

key.name: show-quick-toggle
key.description: Add a Tor toggle to the Quick Settings menu in the system status area.

key.name: control-port
key.description: Port on which Tor exposes its control interface on localhost. Used by the “New Tor identity” action; Tor must have ControlPort enabled.

key.name: control-password
key.description: Password for the Tor control port. Cookie authentication is tried first; this password is used when the cookie cannot be read or is rejected.

key.name: control-cookie-path
key.description: Path to Tor’s control authentication cookie. Leave empty to skip cookie authentication.
